Ahead of the upcoming CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, renowned environmentalist and Magsaysay awardee Dr. Rajendra Singh, popularly known as the ‘Waterman of India’, called upon industrial leaders to abandon resource-depleting manufacturing models and choose sustainable, nature-nourishing growth paradigms.
In a video message addressed to delegates and corporate leaders attending the summit, Dr. Singh urged the global business community to confront the environmental fallout of modern industrialisation. He reminded industrialists that until two centuries ago, India contributed nearly 32% of global gross domestic product (GDP) as a thriving agrarian economy driven by indigenous practices and green jobs.
Expressing deep concern over current economic and ecological trajectories, Dr. Singh noted that rapid and unchecked industrial development has polluted rivers, degraded arable land, and compromised mountain ecosystems, dragging the nation’s global economic share down to approximately 4% while severely denting its overall livability index.
“The convention must deliberate on the precise nature of industry and technology required to make India livable again,” Dr. Singh stressed. He called for a synthesis of modern engineering and science with traditional ecological wisdom, emphasising that industrial processes should work in harmony with environmental conservation rather than at its expense.
Appealing directly to 21st-century industrialists, the environmentalist advocated a decisive shift back to fundamental ecological strengths. He stated that sustainable economic growth could only be sustained if science and technology were harnessed to nourish rivers, land, and communities, thereby helping the nation reclaim its historic position without sacrificing environmental integrity.
